question_text: A 45-year-old man visits the office with complaints of severe pain with urination for 5 days. In addition, he reports having burning discomfort and itchiness at the tip of his penis. He is also concerned regarding a yellow-colored urethral discharge that started a week ago. Before his symptoms began, he states that he had sexual intercourse with multiple partners at different parties organized by the hotel he was staying at. Physical examination shows edema and erythema concentrated around the urethral meatus accompanied by a mucopurulent discharge. Which of the following diagnostic tools will best aid in the identification of the causative agent for his symptoms?
